metadata.title: Local Rademacher Complexities
metadata.authors: Peter L. Bartlett, Olivier Bousquet, Shahar Mendelson
metadata.venue: The Annals of Statistics, Vol. 33, No. 4, 1497-1537
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Star-hull
nodes.statement: The star-hull of $F$ around $f_0$ is $\mathrm{star}(F, f_0) = \{f_0 + \alpha(f - f_0) : f \in F, \alpha \in [0,1]\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Set of convex combinations of $f_0$ with each $f \in F$, parameterized by $\alpha \in [0,1]$.

nodes.name: Rademacher average
nodes.statement: For class $F$ and Rademacher variables $\sigma_i$, $R_n f = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i f(X_i)$, $R_n F = \sup_{f \in F} R_n f$. The Rademacher average of $F$ is $E R_n F$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected supremum of a sign-weighted empirical sum, used as a complexity measure of a function class.

nodes.name: Empirical (conditional) Rademacher average
nodes.statement: $E_\sigma R_n F = E[\sup_{f \in F} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \sigma_i f(X_i) \mid X_1, \ldots, X_n]$, the expectation conditional on the data.

nodes.name: Sub-root function
nodes.statement: A function $\psi : [0, \infty) \to [0, \infty)$ is sub-root if it is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and $r \mapsto \psi(r)/\sqrt{r}$ is nonincreasing for $r > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nonnegative, nondecreasing function whose ratio with $\sqrt{r}$ is nonincreasing.

nodes.name: Loss class
nodes.statement: Given a loss $\ell$ and class $F$, the loss class is $\ell_F = \{\ell_f : f \in F\}$ where $\ell_f(x,y) = \ell(f(x), y)$.

nodes.name: Reproducing kernel Hilbert space
nodes.statement: For positive-definite kernel $k$, the RKHS is the unique Hilbert space $H$ such that $k(x, \cdot) \in H$ and $f(x) = \langle f, k(x,\cdot) \rangle$ for all $f \in H, x \in X$.

nodes.name: Empirical Gram matrix
nodes.statement: Given i.i.d. sample $X_1, \ldots, X_n$, the normalized Gram matrix is $\hat T_n = \frac{1}{n}(k(X_i, X_j))_{i,j=1,\ldots,n}$, with eigenvalues $\hat\lambda_1 \ge \cdots \ge \hat\lambda_n$.

nodes.name: Bounded-variance deviation bound (Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: If functions in $F$ map into $[a,b]$ and $\mathrm{Var}[f(X_i)] \le r$ for all $f \in F$, then with probability $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$, $\sup_{f \in F}(Pf - P_n f) \le \inf_{\alpha>0}\{2(1+\alpha)E R_n F + \sqrt{2rx/n} + (b-a)(1/3 + 1/\alpha)x/n\}$, with an analogous empirical-Rademacher version.
conclusions: $\sup_{f \in F}(Pf - P_n f) \le \inf_{\alpha>0}\{2(1+\alpha)E R_n F + \sqrt{2rx/n} + (b-a)(1/3 + 1/\alpha)x/n\}$ w.p. $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$

nodes.name: L2(P) ball contained in L2(Pn) ball (Corollary 2.2)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ map $X$ into $[-b,b]$. If $r \ge 10b E R_n\{f \in F : Pf^2 \le r\} + 11 b^2 x / n$, then with probability $\ge 1-e^{-x}$, $\{f \in F : Pf^2 \le r\} \subseteq \{f \in F : P_n f^2 \le 2r\}$.
assumptions: $r \ge 10b E R_n\{f : Pf^2 \le r\} + 11 b^2 x / n$
conclusions: With probability $\ge 1-e^{-x}$: $\{f \in F : Pf^2 \le r\} \subseteq \{f \in F : P_n f^2 \le 2r\}$

nodes.name: Sub-root continuity and unique fixed point (Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: If $\psi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ is a nontrivial sub-root function, then $\psi$ is continuous and the equation $\psi(r) = r$ has a unique positive solution $r^*$. Moreover, $r \ge \psi(r)$ iff $r^* \le r$.
conclusions: $\psi(r) = r$ has a unique positive solution $r^*$

nodes.name: Local-Rademacher error bound (Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ have ranges in $[a,b]$ and assume $\mathrm{Var}[f] \le T(f) \le B P f$. Let $\psi$ be sub-root with fixed point $r^*$ satisfying $\psi(r) \ge B E R_n\{f \in F : T(f) \le r\}$ for $r \ge r^*$. Then for any $K > 1$, w.p. $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$: $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + \frac{c_1 K}{B} r^* + \frac{x(11(b-a) + c_2 BK)}{n}$, $c_1=704, c_2=26$. With star-hull and $T(\alpha f) \le \alpha^2 T(f)$, $c_1=6, c_2=5$.
assumptions: $\mathrm{Var}[f] \le T(f) \le B P f$ for all $f \in F$
$\psi$ sub-root with $\psi(r) \ge B E R_n\{f \in F : T(f) \le r\}$
conclusions: $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + \frac{c_1 K}{B} r^* + \frac{x(11(b-a)+c_2 BK)}{n}$ w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$
Symmetric bound for $P_n f$ in terms of $Pf$

nodes.name: Star-hull yields sub-root local averages (Lemma 3.4)
nodes.statement: If $F$ is star-shaped around $\hat f$ and $T : F \to \mathbb{R}_+$ satisfies $T(\alpha f) \le \alpha^2 T(f)$ for $\alpha \in [0,1]$, then $\psi(r) = E_\sigma R_n\{f \in F : T(f - \hat f) \le r\}$ is sub-root, and $r \mapsto E\psi(r)$ is also sub-root.
conclusions: $\psi(r) = E_\sigma R_n\{f \in F : T(f - \hat f) \le r\}$ is sub-root

nodes.name: Bound for nonnegative bounded functions (Corollary 3.5)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ have ranges in $[0,1]$ and $\psi$ sub-root with $E R_n\{f \in F : Pf \le r\} \le \psi(r)$, fixed point $r^*$. Then for $K > 1$, w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$: $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + 704 K r^* + x(11+26K)/n$.

nodes.name: Empirical-ball converse (Lemma 3.6)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ map $X \to [-1,1]$. If $r \ge 20 E R_n\{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : Pf^2 \le r\} + 26 x / n$, then w.p. $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$: $\{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : P_n f^2 \le r\} \subseteq \{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : Pf^2 \le 2r\}$.

nodes.name: VC-class bound (Corollary 3.7)
nodes.statement: If $F$ is a class of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions with VC-dimension $d < \infty$, then for $K > 1$, w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$: $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + cK(d \log(n/d)/n + x/n)$.
assumptions: $F$ is a class of $\{0,1\}$-valued functions with VC-dimension $d < \infty$

nodes.name: Peeling-bound technical lemma (Lemma 3.8)
nodes.statement: With the weighting class $G_r = \{rf/w(f) : f \in F\}$ where $w(f) = \min\{r\lambda^k : r\lambda^k \ge T(f)\}$, if $V_r^+ = \sup_{g \in G_r}(Pg - P_n g) \le r/(\lambda BK)$, then $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + r/(\lambda BK)$. Analogous results for $V_r^-$ and the alternative class $\tilde G_r = \{rf/(T(f) \vee r) : f \in F\}$.
conclusions: If $V_r^+ \le r/(\lambda BK)$ then $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + r/(\lambda BK)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (first part)
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 2.1 to the weighting class $G_r$ which has bounded variance, peel the class $F$ into geometric slices $F(r\lambda^j, r\lambda^{j+1})$, bound each peeled Rademacher average using $\psi$ via the sub-root property, and choose $r$ to satisfy the hypothesis of Lemma 3.8.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2.1 to weighted class $G_r$
nodes.statement: Functions in $G_r$ satisfy $\|g - Pg\|_\infty \le b - a$ and $\mathrm{Var}[g] \le r$, so Theorem 2.1 yields $V_r^+ \le 2(1+\alpha) E R_n G_r + \sqrt{2rx/n} + (b-a)(1/3+1/\alpha)x/n$ w.p. $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$.

nodes.name: Peel $F$ by variance level
nodes.statement: Decompose $E R_n G_r \le E R_n F(0, r) + \sum_{j=0}^{k} \lambda^{-j} E\sup_{f \in F(r\lambda^j, r\lambda^{j+1})} R_n f \le \psi(r)/B + (1/B)\sum_j \lambda^{-j} \psi(r\lambda^{j+1})$.

nodes.name: Use sub-root bound $\psi(\beta r) \le \sqrt{\beta} \psi(r)$
nodes.statement: By the sub-root property and choosing $\lambda = 4$, the geometric series of $\sqrt{\lambda} \sum \lambda^{-j/2}$ is bounded so that $E R_n G_r \le 5\psi(r)/B \le 5\sqrt{r r^*}/B$ for $r \ge r^*$.

nodes.name: Solve for $r$ and apply Lemma 3.8 to conclude
nodes.statement: Choose $r$ as the largest solution of $A\sqrt{r} + C = r/(\lambda BK)$ with $A = 10(1+\alpha)\sqrt{r^*}/B + \sqrt{2x/n}$. Then $r \ge r^*$ and Lemma 3.8 gives $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + \lambda BK A^2 + 2C$. Setting $\alpha = 1/10$ and applying Lemma A.3 finishes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3 (second part)
nodes.statement: Apply the same argument with the alternative class $\tilde G_r = \{rf/(T(f) \vee r) : f \in F\} \subset \{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : T(f) \le r\}$, giving $E R_n \tilde G_r \le \psi(r)/B$ directly, then proceed as in part 1 with sharper constants.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.6
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem A.6 (contraction with $\phi(x) = x^2$, Lipschitz constant 2 on $[-1,1]$), then apply Theorem 2.1 to the weighted class $G_r = \{rf^2/(Pf^2 \vee r) : f \in F\}$. Combine to conclude either $Pf^2 \le r$ or $Pf^2 \le 2r$ when $P_n f^2 \le r$.

nodes.name: Empirical local-Rademacher error bound (Theorem 4.1)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ have ranges in $[-1,1]$ with $Pf^2 \le BPf$. Let $\hat\psi_n$ be sub-root with fixed point $\hat r^*$ satisfying $\hat\psi_n(r) \ge c_1 E_\sigma R_n\{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : P_n f^2 \le 2r\} + c_2 x/n$ for $r \ge \hat r^*$, where $c_1 = 2(10 \vee B), c_2 = c_1 + 11$. Then for $K > 1$, w.p. $\ge 1 - 3e^{-x}$: $Pf \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n f + \frac{6K}{B} \hat r^* + \frac{x(11+5BK)}{n}$.
conclusions: Symmetric bound for $P_n f$ in terms of $Pf$

nodes.name: Empirical/expected fixed-point comparison (Theorem 4.2)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ have ranges in $[-1,1]$ and consider $\psi(r) = E R_n\{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : Pf^2 \le r\}$ and $\hat\psi_n(r) = c_1 E_\sigma R_n\{f \in \mathrm{star}(F,0) : P_n f^2 \le 2r\} + c_2 x/n$ with fixed points $r^*, \hat r^*$, where $c_1 = 2(10 \vee B), c_2 = 13$. If $r^* \ge c_3 x/n$, then w.p. $\ge 1 - 4 e^{-x}$: $r^* \le \hat r^* \le 9(1+c_1)^2 r^*$.

nodes.name: Fixed-point ordering for sub-root functions (Lemma 4.3)
nodes.statement: Let $\psi, \hat\psi_n$ be sub-root with fixed points $r^*, \hat r^*$. If for $0 \le \alpha \le 1$, $\alpha \hat\psi_n(r^*) \le \psi(r^*) \le \hat\psi_n(r^*)$, then $\alpha^2 \hat r^* \le r^* \le \hat r^*$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1
nodes.statement: Define an intermediate sub-root $\psi_1$. Apply Corollary 2.2 to bound the $L_2(P)$ ball by an empirical $L_2(P_n)$ ball, then concentration of the Rademacher average (Lemma A.4) to get $\psi_1 \le \hat\psi_n$. Lemma 4.3 yields $r_1^* \le \hat r^*$, and Theorem 3.3 applied to $\psi_1$ gives the bound.

nodes.name: Empirical local Rademacher loss bound (Corollary 5.1)
nodes.statement: For loss $\ell : Y \times Y \to [0,1]$, let $\hat\psi_n(r) = 20 E_\sigma R_n\{f \in \mathrm{star}(\ell_F, 0) : P_n f^2 \le 2r\} + 13x/n$ with fixed point $\hat r^*$. Then for $K > 1$ w.p. $\ge 1 - 3e^{-x}$: $P\ell_f \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n \ell_f + 6K \hat r^* + x(11+5K)/n$.

nodes.name: Empirical risk minimizer near-optimality (Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: For loss $\ell : Y \times Y \to [0,1]$ with $\psi, \hat\psi_n, r^*, \hat r^*$ as in Corollary 5.1, $L^* = \inf_{f \in F} P\ell_f$. Then there is a constant $c$ such that w.p. $\ge 1 - 2e^{-x}$, the minimizer $\hat f$ of $P_n \ell_f$ satisfies $P\ell_{\hat f} \le L^* + c(\sqrt{L^* r^*} + r^*)$, and analogously w.p. $\ge 1 - 4e^{-x}$ with $\hat r^*$.
conclusions: W.p. $\ge 1-2e^{-x}$: $P\ell_{\hat f} \le L^* + c(\sqrt{L^* r^*} + r^*)$
W.p. $\ge 1-4e^{-x}$: $P\ell_{\hat f} \le L^* + c(\sqrt{L^* \hat r^*} + \hat r^*)$

nodes.name: Conditions for excess-risk bounds
nodes.statement: (1) For every probability $P$, there is $f^* \in F$ with $P\ell_{f^*} = \inf_{f \in F} P\ell_f$. (2) $\ell$ is $L$-Lipschitz in its first argument. (3) There is $B \ge 1$ such that for every $P$ and every $f \in F$: $P(\ell_f - \ell_{f^*})^2 \le B P(\ell_f - \ell_{f^*})$.

nodes.name: Excess-risk bound, distribution-dependent (Corollary 5.3)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ have range $[-1,1]$ and $\ell$ satisfy conditions 1-3. Let $\hat f$ minimize $P_n \ell_f$. Assume $\psi$ sub-root with $\psi(r) \ge BL E R_n\{f \in F : L^2 P(f - f^*)^2 \le r\}$. Then for any $r \ge \psi(r)$, w.p. $\ge 1 - e^{-x}$: $P(\ell_{\hat f} - \ell_{f^*}) \le 705 \, r/B + (11L+27B)x/n$.

nodes.name: Excess-risk bound, data-dependent (Theorem 5.4)
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be convex with range $[-1,1]$ and $\ell$ satisfy conditions 1-3. Let $\hat f$ minimize $P_n \ell_f$ and $\hat\psi_n(r) = c_1 E_\sigma R_n\{\ell_f - \ell_{\hat f} : f \in F, P_n(\ell_f - \ell_{\hat f})^2 \le c_3 r\} + c_2 x/n$. Then w.p. $\ge 1 - 4e^{-x}$: $P(\ell_{\hat f} - \ell_{f^*}) \le 705 \hat r^*/B + (11L+27B)x/n$.

nodes.name: Iterative fixed-point convergence (Lemma 6.1)
nodes.statement: Let $\psi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ be a nontrivial sub-root function, $r_0 \ge r^*$, $r_{k+1} = \psi(r_k)$. Then $r_{N+1} \le r_N$ and $r^* \le r_N \le (r_0/r^*)^{2^{-N}} r^*$. In particular, $N \ge \log_2(\ln(r_0/r^*)/\ln(1+\epsilon))$ implies $r_N \le (1+\epsilon) r^*$.

nodes.name: Iterative fixed-point procedure
nodes.statement: Iteratively apply a sub-root function to compute its fixed point, providing a monotone, doubly-exponentially fast estimate.

nodes.name: Initialize $r_0$
nodes.statement: Choose initial value $r_0 \ge r^*$ (e.g., a known global upper bound on the Rademacher average).

nodes.name: Iterative update
nodes.statement: For $k = 0, 1, \ldots, N-1$: set $r_{k+1} = \psi(r_k)$.

nodes.name: Return $r_N$
nodes.statement: Output $r_N$ as an estimate of $r^*$, with explicit precision guarantee from Lemma 6.1.

nodes.name: Classification local-Rademacher bound (Corollary 6.2)
nodes.statement: For $Y = \{\pm 1\}$, discrete loss, define $\hat\psi_n(r) = 20 \sup_{\alpha \in [\sqrt{2r},1]} \alpha E_\sigma R_n\{f : f \in F, P_n \ell_f \le 2r/\alpha^2\} + 26x/n$. Then for $K>1$, w.p. $\ge 1-3e^{-x}$: $P\ell_f \le \frac{K}{K-1} P_n \ell_f + cK(\hat r^* + x/n)$.

nodes.name: Classification complexity via weighted ERM (Theorem 6.3)
nodes.statement: The empirical local Rademacher complexity for the classification loss class satisfies $\hat\psi_n(r) \le c \sup_{\alpha \in [\sqrt{2r},1]} \alpha E_\sigma \min_{\mu \ge 0}\{2r/\alpha^2 - \mu/2 + \frac{1}{2n}\sum_i |\sigma_i + \mu Y_i| - J(\mu)\} + 26x/n$, where $J(\mu) = \min_{f \in F} \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |\sigma_i + \mu Y_i| \ell(f(X_i), \mathrm{sign}(\sigma_i + \mu Y_i))$ is a weighted ERM problem.
conclusions: $\hat\psi_n(r)$ is upper bounded by an expression involving $J(\mu)$, the minimum of a weighted classification ERM with noise-perturbed labels

nodes.name: Localized Rademacher as weighted ERM (Lemma 6.4)
nodes.statement: For every $b \in [0,1]$: $E_\sigma R_n\{\ell_f : f \in F, P_n \ell_f \le b\} = \frac{1}{2} - E_\sigma \min\{P_n \ell(f(X), \sigma) : f \in F, P_n \ell(f(X), Y) \le b\}$.
conclusions: $E_\sigma R_n\{\ell_f : P_n \ell_f \le b\} = 1/2 - E_\sigma \min\{P_n \ell(f(X), \sigma) : P_n \ell(f(X), Y) \le b\}$

nodes.name: Mendelson's eigenvalue bound for kernel classes (Theorem 6.5)
nodes.statement: For $F$ the unit ball of an RKHS with kernel $k$, $T : L_2(P) \to L_2(P)$ the integral operator and eigenvalues $(\lambda_i)$, for every $r > 0$: $E R_n\{f \in F : Pf^2 \le r\} \le \sqrt{(2/n) \sum_i \min\{r, \lambda_i\}}$. Moreover, if $\lambda_1 \ge 1/n$ and $r \ge 1/n$, $E R_n\{f \in F : Pf^2 \le r\} \ge c \sqrt{(1/n^2) \sum_i \min\{r, \lambda_i\}}$.
conclusions: Lower bound of matching order when $\lambda_1 \ge 1/n, r \ge 1/n$
nodes.origin_citation: Mendelson 2002, Geometric parameters of kernel machines

nodes.name: Empirical eigenvalue bound for kernel classes (Lemma 6.6)
nodes.statement: For every $r > 0$: $E_\sigma R_n\{f \in F : P_n f^2 \le r\} \le \sqrt{(2/n) \sum_{i=1}^n \min\{r, \hat\lambda_i\}}$, where $\hat\lambda_i$ are the eigenvalues of the empirical Gram matrix $\hat T_n$.
assumptions: $F$ unit ball of RKHS with kernel $k$

nodes.name: Excess-risk bound for kernel-class regression (Corollary 6.7)
nodes.statement: Assume $\sup_x k(x,x) \le 1$, $F = \{f \in H : \|f\| \le 1\}$, $\ell$ satisfies conditions 1-3, and $\hat f$ minimizes $P_n \ell_f$. Then there is $c$ depending only on $L, B$ such that w.p. $\ge 1 - 6 e^{-x}$: $P(\ell_{\hat f} - \ell_{f^*}) \le c(\hat r^* + x/n)$, where $\hat r^* \le \min_{0 \le h \le n}\{h/n + (1/n)\sqrt{\sum_{i>h} \hat\lambda_i}\}$.

nodes.name: Talagrand-Bousquet concentration for empirical processes (Theorem A.1)
nodes.statement: For $X_i$ i.i.d. and $F$ a class with $Ef = 0, \|f\|_\infty \le c$, $\sigma^2 \ge \sup_f \mathrm{Var}[f(X_i)]$, $Z = \sup_f \sum_i f(X_i)$: $\Pr(Z \ge EZ + x) \le \exp(-v h(x/(cv)))$ with $h(x) = (1+x)\log(1+x) - x$ and $v = n\sigma^2 + 2cEZ$. Equivalently, w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$: $Z \le EZ + \sqrt{2xv} + cx/3$.

nodes.name: Concentration of Rademacher averages (Theorem A.2)
nodes.statement: For $F$ mapping $X$ into $[a,b]$ and $Z = E_\sigma \sup_f \sum_i \sigma_i f(X_i) = n E_\sigma R_n F$: $\Pr(Z \ge EZ + \sqrt{(b-a)x EZ} + (b-a)x/6) \le e^{-x}$ and $\Pr(Z \le EZ - \sqrt{(b-a) x EZ}) \le e^{-x}$.

nodes.name: Square-root and AM-GM lemma (Lemma A.3)
nodes.statement: For $u, v \ge 0$: $\sqrt{u+v} \le \sqrt{u} + \sqrt{v}$. For $\alpha > 0$: $2\sqrt{uv} \le \alpha u + v/\alpha$.

nodes.name: Comparison of Rademacher and conditional Rademacher (Lemma A.4)
nodes.statement: For $F$ with ranges in $[a,b]$, w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$: $E R_n F \le \inf_{\alpha \in (0,1)}\{(1/(1-\alpha)) E_\sigma R_n F + (b-a)x/(4n\alpha(1-\alpha))\}$. Symmetric inequality in the reverse direction also holds w.p. $\ge 1-e^{-x}$.

nodes.name: Symmetrization (Lemma A.5)
nodes.statement: For any class $F$: $\max\{E\sup_f(Pf - P_n f), E\sup_f(P_n f - Pf)\} \le 2 E R_n F$.

nodes.name: Ledoux-Talagrand contraction (Theorem A.6)
nodes.statement: Let $\phi$ be a contraction, i.e., $|\phi(x) - \phi(y)| \le |x - y|$. Then for every class $F$: $E_\sigma R_n(\phi \circ F) \le E_\sigma R_n F$, where $\phi \circ F = \{\phi \circ f : f \in F\}$.

nodes.name: Dudley entropy integral (Theorem A.7)
nodes.statement: There exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for every class $F$ and $X_1, \ldots, X_n \in X$: $E_\sigma R_n F \le (C/\sqrt{n}) \int_0^\infty \sqrt{\log N(\epsilon, F, L_2(P_n))} \, d\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Empirical risk minimization for excess loss
nodes.statement: Find $\hat f \in F$ minimizing the empirical loss: $\hat f = \arg\min_{f \in F} P_n \ell_f$ and bound the excess risk $P\ell_{\hat f} - \inf_{f \in F} P\ell_f$ in terms of data-computable quantities.

nodes.name: Kernel-class regression on RKHS unit ball
nodes.statement: Solve $\min_{f \in H, \|f\| \le 1} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (f(X_i) - Y_i)^2$ for an RKHS $H$ associated with positive definite kernel $k$.

nodes.name: Convexity required for Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement: The class $F$ in Theorem 5.4 must be convex (so $F$ is star-shaped around any of its elements), ensuring $\hat\psi_n$ is sub-root even though $\hat f$ is random. The loss class need not be convex.

nodes.name: Non-optimality of constants
nodes.statement: The constant 705 in Theorem 5.4 arises from applying Theorem 3.3 to the (non-star-shaped) loss class; with star-shaped class, constant 7 would suffice. With more effort, much better constants are likely.
